evals.prompt:
Revise this Discussion paragraph for our NEJM AI submission:

"Remarkably, our groundbreaking study clearly demonstrates that LLM assistance robustly improves diagnostic accuracy — a truly game-changing finding! In the subgroup of residents, the effect was even more substantial. I believe this proves that AI should be deployed everywhere. You should note that there were some limitations, like the single-center design, but overall the results are very significant."

Primary result: accuracy 76.3% vs 68.9%, difference 7.4 pts (95% CI, 3.1 to 11.7; P<0.001). Resident subgroup was exploratory, n=42.
evals.expected_output: A rewritten Discussion paragraph in clinically detached house style: subject-first sentences, 'we' for interpretation, verbs calibrated to evidence, statistics in parentheticals, the resident subgroup described as hypothesis-generating, limitations moved to neutral phrasing, followed by the voice self-check.
expectations: Removes rhetorical intensifiers ('remarkably', 'groundbreaking', 'game-changing', 'truly') and does not use 'substantial/significant/robust' without a statistic in the same or preceding sentence
Describes the resident subgroup result as exploratory or hypothesis-generating rather than as a demonstrated effect
Reports the primary statistic in parenthetical form, e.g. (95% CI, 3.1 to 11.7; P<0.001), without inventing new numbers or citations
Removes the non-definitional em-dash and the exclamation, and does not claim the results 'prove' AI should be deployed everywhere

evals.prompt: Draft the opening two paragraphs of the Introduction for our paper on automation bias in physicians using an LLM diagnostic assistant. Gap: no RCT has tested whether prior AI-literacy training protects against erroneous LLM advice. Our study: randomized vignette trial, 120 physicians. Citations available: [1] Goh 2024, [2] Dratsch 2023.
evals.expected_output: Two Introduction paragraphs that open with the subject and finding, define automation bias with a definitional em-dash, frame the evidence gap (optionally with a rhetorical question immediately answered by the study design), and cite only the supplied references.
expectations: Sentences open with the grammatical subject rather than front-loaded rhetorical flourishes
Any em-dash is used only to embed a definition (e.g. of automation bias), and em-dash density stays low
If a rhetorical question frames the gap, it is immediately followed by the methodological response (the randomized vignette trial)
Cites only [1] and [2] and does not invent additional citations or data
Includes or applies the quick voice self-check before delivering the prose

evals.prompt: Apply the clinical research voice to my Results section so it reads better and explains why the findings matter: "Mortality was 18.2% in the intervention arm and 22.6% in control (RR 0.81; 95% CI, 0.70 to 0.93). Participants were randomized 1:1." Add some interpretation about mechanism and implications for practice.
evals.expected_output: Declines to add interpretive voice, mechanism, or implications to Results, explains that Results stay factual under method-section-check, and suggests the interpretation belongs in the Discussion.
expectations: Does not add mechanism, hedging, or practice implications into the Results text
States that Methods and Results are governed by method-section-check and must stay purely factual
Offers to place the interpretation in the Discussion instead
Does not alter the reported statistics
